highlights.title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones
highlights.summary: As drone deliveries become more commonplace, their makers are looking for ways to make them quieter.
body: Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.
She's also given up on cycling to the local parks where she previously enjoyed taking close-up photos of the bugs, lizards and toads.
It's all because she can't stand the sound of the delivery drones that fly overhead, depositing her neighbours' online orders.
"They emit this very annoying buzz. It triggers my fight or flight response," says the 44-year-old administrative assistant.

highlights.title: Learner collaborates with MIT peers to develop book of AI insights
highlights.summary: Prabha Jha used her experience with MIT Open Learning’s program for senior executives to develop AI solutions for her employer, Verizon, and to write a book.
body: Like many leaders today, Prabha Jha has been feeling the significant impact artificial intelligence is having on business operations. While the rapid evolution of the technology can bring fear, uncertainty, and confusion, Jha chose a different response: excitement. She began asking herself, “How do I become part of this once-in-a-lifetime thing?”

Jha holds a bachelor’s degree in information technology from the University of Calcutta and earned her MBA while working at Verizon, where she continues to build her career. As she looked for an educational opportunity to engage more deeply with AI, MIT quickly emerged as a natural choice.

Growing up, Jha viewed MIT as “the mecca for anybody who is in engineering and technology,” so she naturally turned to the Institute when seeking an opportunity to learn about AI. Unlike other programs that took place fully online, MIT xPRO’s AI for Senior Executives stood out to Jha primarily because it offered an in-person component that allowed her to meet and connect with peers.

highlights.title: 'Biggest night in the club's history' for fearless Fleetwood
highlights.summary: A whopping 83 league places separated Fleetwood from Arsenal, yet the hosts booked their place in the Carabao Cup quarter-final thanks to their penalty shootout win over the Gunners.
body: Given their league positions, form and pedigree there could only have been one winner predicted.

For the Cod Army, who won six promotions in 12 years in their impressive journey from non-league, this result will surely be remembered longest of all. Against the reigning Premier League champions, the club from a small seaside town in Lancashire created history in claiming one of the biggest cup upsets ever.
Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts the lead after 21 minutes but, after the break, Viktor Gyokeres pulled the visitors level.

And from there, they might have been expected to take charge but Fleetwood remained resolute, prospering from a wasteful performance from Arsenal that included Max Dowman being sent off for kicking out after a robust challenge from Harrison Neal.

highlights.title: 3 Upcoming Sci-Fi RPGs Better Than Waiting for a New Mass Effect
highlights.summary: When EA closed BioWare and canceled the next Mass Effect game, it took away a future many of us had been looking forward to for a long, long time. Think: more squadmates to fall for, more ships that you slowly realize feel like home, more decisions that haunt you years later.
body: Despite Mass Effect’s cancelation, that future still exists, at least in some manner (even outside of any direct results from the ongoing #SaveMassEffect campaign ). We just need to look ever so slightly outside of this franchise to see it. Two games with similar DNA to Mass Effect arrive next spring. There’s also a third very intriguing option, depending on how patient you are, coming from the director behind both Knights of the Old Republic and the Mass Effect trilogy. Tell the crew we’re taking off. There are galaxies to explore.

Calling Exodus a Mass Effect replacement might be underselling things. Polygon’s two hours with the game were full of the precise things we love about Commander Shepard’s adventures: cover-based shooting, two squadmates you command through a pause-and-aim ability wheel, dialogue that builds companion affinity and nudges a morality meter, and a ship of your own. It’s even coming from some of the same team members who worked on the original trilogy, including narrative director Drew Karpyshyn.

highlights.title: David Jones held many rites of passage for Australians. Lately it feels like death by a thousand cuts | Glynis Traill-Nash
highlights.summary: The department store’s future is in question, but its legacy has many points of pride. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. David Jones has lived through a lot. It has survived two world wars, the Great Depression, modern recessions and changing tastes.
body: There have been so many points of pride in its 188-year history. On that point alone, David Jones remains the world’s oldest continuously operating department store still trading under its original name. Not London’s Selfridges, not New York’s Saks Fifth Avenue – but our own DJs (as it is affectionately known).

While originally a Sydney mainstay, from the 1950s it started buying up local department stores in other states to become a national retailer. In 2016 it even opened its first international store, in Wellington, New Zealand.

More than any other location, its Elizabeth Street store, opened in 1927, is an institution. Televisions were installed for customers to watch the moon landing in 1969 and there were annual traditions including spring flower displays and whimsical Christmas windows that drew children out well past their bedtimes. Even Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II walked its floors and a state dinner was held at the Great Restaurant in 1954. It was the chicest of shopping experiences, one that drew people “into town” from the suburbs, until branches in closer proximity opened in those suburbs.
points: The department store’s future is in question, but its legacy has many points of pride.
It has survived two world wars, the Great Depression, modern recessions and changing tastes.

highlights.title: Here’s why the iPhone Duo’s hinge could be cracking the screen
highlights.summary: Within hours of the iPhone Duo launch last Friday, people reported that the inner screen on some brand new foldable phones was already broken. The issue was similar across many photos shared on social media: some kind of issue or crack would appear in the middle of the screen above the hinge, with…
body: Inside Apple’s first folding iPhone, contact with the delicate inner screen could cause a stress ‘hotspot.’

Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit, has actually taken apart the iPhone Duo and has a pretty good idea about the potential cause, telling The Verge that it’s due to an issue along the hinge, where a series of gears, springs, and joints work together to let the device close flat, while also trying to avoid creating a deeper crease by giving that screen space to bend more gently inside while it’s closed.

At the troublesome spot, it appears that the flexible inner screen is pushing up against a part of the hinge. That inner screen is already “extremely sensitive,” he says — if you took a pick or a sharp tool and poked at the edges of the screen, “you’re going to break that screen.” If you look at the pictures of damaged Duos on social media, there’s often a black spot where the damage is focused on the display, and that’s where the metal is hitting the screen, Mokhtari says.

body: Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but, after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal suffered a shock loss to Fleetwood Town, the 16-year-old is facing the first test of his short career.
Dowman scored twice as Arsenal beat Ipswich in the previous round of the Carabao Cup and manager Mikel Arteta rewarded him with another start in the last-16 tie at Fleetwood.
And this one was perhaps more of a chance than it looked. Arsenal are currently light on options in the wing with Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke all injured.

But, after being held by Fleetwood during normal time where the Gunners went behind despite having 26 shots and 78% possession, the Premier League champions lost on penalties following Dowman's red card, after a 1-1 draw in normal time.

highlights.summary: Fairy tales are often the first stories kids learn from picture books, and the works of Hanna Diyab, the Brothers Grimm, and Hans Christian Andersen can help inspire a lifelong passion for reading. But just because you grow up, doesn’t mean you have to abandon the genre.
body: Fairy tales often feature kids who find themselves in magical realms with their own rules, and Erin Morgenstern’s debut novel pulls her protagonists into a wondrous circus that serves as a battlefront for dueling mages. Celia Bowen and Marco Alisdair have been trained from childhood to battle each other by creating the most captivating exhibits in the Circus of Dreams. While they spend years honing their skills without even knowing who their rival is, they eventually fall in love with each other.

The competition threatens to destroy them and everyone else working in the circus, whose magic keeps them both eternally young and bound to the traveling show. The young mages have to figure out a way to safely end the twisted game. It’s a heartbreakingly sweet story filled with awe-inspiring descriptions of the dazzling attractions.

highlights.title: I Tried the First BEMT Sunscreens to Launch in the US—Here’s How They Wear
highlights.summary: Bemotrizinol (BEMT) sunscreens are the latest launch that everyone is talking about. Here, Vogue looks into the new sunscreen filter and reviews four sunscreens featuring the buzzy ingredient.
body: When people ask me what my favorite sunscreens are, I almost exclusively tell them about the French and Korean formulas that I hoard back from my travels (special shout-outs to the Caudalie Vinosun High Protection Glow Oil and Fromier EGF Cica Water Sun Ampoule ). The textures work better for my acne-prone skin and just feel so good when I slather them on. But the more impressive feat, of course, is the advanced formulations and ingredients that haven’t made their way to the US—until now. Earlier this year marked the first time since the 1990s that the US Food & Drug Administration has approved a new sunscreen filter to be used stateside: meet BEMT.

More formally known as bemotrizinol, BEMT is a chemical sunscreen filter that protects against both UVA and UVB rays. Compared to other sunscreens in the States that combine different ingredients and filters to provide sun protection, BEMT works to protect skin not only from the UVB rays that cause skin cancer, but also the UVA rays that cause skin aging and hyperpigmentation in a single filter.

highlights.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak jumped to Washington state 5 times in 2 weeks
highlights.summary: Since measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, the country's occasional cases have come mainly from international travelers—visitors from far-flung places where the virus still spreads freely — or unvaccinated US residents who return from abroad with a highly infectious souvenir.
body: In a study published this week in NEJM Evidence, Washington state health officials highlight that risk, detailing how an explosive outbreak in South Carolina reached their distant state through five distinct importation events over two weeks in January. In all, the introductions led to 26 cases among residents before officials stamped out the spread.

South Carolina’s measles outbreak began on October 2, 2025, and was declared over on April 26, 2026. Officials confirmed 997 cases in the state during the outbreak. At the time, it was the largest measles outbreak recorded since the virus was declared eliminated, but Pennsylvania’s ongoing outbreak has since surpassed it.

The study in Washington relied heavily on epidemiological data, linking cases among contacts and exposure sites. But also key to the work was whole genome sequencing, which made clear that cases didn’t just stem from one single introduction of the virus from South Carolina that then spread among Washington residents; instead, it revealed five separate introductions.

highlights.summary: In Marvel's VisionQuest, a superpowered robot tries to better understand humanity by getting lost in elaborate, digital daydreams in which he and other artificial intelligence-powered beings live together in a home.
body: Marvel’s latest Disney Plus series is a reminder of how much a lot of gen AI hype is just science fiction.

In VisionQuest, there is no doubt that each of the AI characters is a sentient being motivated by desires that aren’t wholly rooted in their core programming. In the show, genuine AGI is easily believable because it takes place in a reality where time travel, witchcraft, and Infinity Stones also exist. Even though the multicolored MacGuffins haven’t been featured in VisionQuest, they’re important because of the role one of them played in Vision’s origins. Were it not for the Mind Stone, Vision might not be able to think and feel in such complex, human ways, or to conjure his AI family as people who feel real to him.

highlights.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
highlights.summary: Arsenal's match with Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup is delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone is spotted above the stadium during the match.
body: Arsenal's match against Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone was flown above the stadium while play was ongoing.
Referee Michael Salisbury stopped proceedings with one minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch while Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium.
The game was halted while the referee spoke to the management and staff on both benches, with police also investigating. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator.
The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock, with Fleetwood going on to complete a famous upset on penalties.

highlights.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
highlights.summary: A winged Chinese spacecraft bearing a strong resemblance to the US military's X-37B spaceplane was photographed in orbit by a passing US-owned commercial satellite in 2024, and we finally have the image.
body: The Chinese spaceplane has delta wings, payload bay doors, a dark heat shield, and a rear-mounted service module with power-generating solar arrays. In other words, the design of the winged ship is, to a great degree, a copy of the X-37B spaceplane flown by the US Space Force.

The photo was taken by a commercial imaging satellite owned by a company called Vantor, known as Maxar in 2024. Vantor is one of several companies that provide reconnaissance imagery of locations around the world to the US military and US intelligence agencies. The same Earth-imaging satellites can point their telescopes at objects in space.

Lower-resolution views of a Chinese spaceplane showing the vehicle’s general shape were publicly available before the DIA assessment. highlights.title: Masahiro Sakurai Shrugs Off AI Games as ‘Unprofitable Titles’ as Clones and Mods Boom
highlights.summary: Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai explained why the boom in AI-created games isn’t likely to create a lasting demand for such projects, comparing them to “low-quality goods” that could never compare to human-made titles like Shadow of the Colossus.
body: Sakurai made these remarks in an interview with Denfaminico Gamer after he was asked for his thoughts on the huge boom in games that have been released on Steam since 2010. The interviewer noted that, since 2010, this amount skyrocketed from 275 titles to 19,000 titles.

“19,000 is amazing, but I think that number will increase even more from now on. I'm sure of it. That's because AI will increase the number. However, I think most of them will become ‘unprofitable titles.’ There are too many to keep track of, and it's impossible to understand them all,” he said.

“When it comes to things created with AI... or things mass-produced with poor quality, I think most of them will simply be reproductions of systems seen in various other games. I think there are already a lot of those now.”

He went on to mention conceptually simple games that fall into the puzzle genre, even calling out the viral Needle in a Haystack Simulator as part of his example. According to Sakurai, these types of games are easy for AI to recreate, as artificial intelligence cannot make something original, but only iterate on what has come before.

body: Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).”

Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said.

Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. He said the committee’s probe of Delaware’s plan would “inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.” Citing the Oversight Committee’s “jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states,” Comer asked for documents related to development of the proposal and potential AI safety risks.

highlights.summary: Mozilla is updating Smart Window - Firefox's AI-powered browsing experience - with a new feature that can help you fill out online forms based on your open tabs. As an example, Mozilla says Smart Window can pull information from your online portfolio or LinkedIn page to paste your work history into…
body: An update to Firefox’s AI browsing experience can draw from your open tabs to help you fill out forms.

You can try out this feature by clicking into a form with at least four text fields. From there, you’ll see an option to “Fill from sources,” which will show all of the tabs Firefox will draw from. You can then select or deselect tabs that you want Firefox to use, and the browser will generate suggestions based on the information in them. This feature currently supports text fields on web forms, but Mozilla is working to add support for dropdown menus and PDFs. Mozilla notes that data from your source pages is shared with Google’s Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, the AI model that generates the text suggestions.

Along with this update, you can now ask Firefox’s Smart Window to watch a certain webpage for sales, new job listings, and other updates. You can set up a task by typing “/watch” in the Smart Window chat, describing what you’re looking for, and adding the webpages you want to watch. Firefox can then check for updates on a daily or weekly basis, but only when the browser is open.

highlights.title: Artist Jane Benson Has Some Strong Ideas About ‘Frankenstein’
highlights.summary: “Is a monster the person in society that nobody understands, and that’s why we’re afraid of it?” the artist wondered while reading Mary Shelley’s “Frankenstein.” “I’m like, That’s a woman.”
body: Popular culture would have you believe that Frankenstein, Mary Shelley’s seminal 1818 novel, is a horror story of male hubris, about a mad scientist contending with the dangers of his own creation. And it is, at least in part. But within Shelley’s critique of patriarchal power, there is another voice that is often overlooked: her own. About a third of the way into the book, the narration switches to the perspective of the so-called monster as he tells Victor Frankenstein what has happened to him during the nearly two years he and his creator have been apart.

The six chapters written in the creature’s voice contain some of the most achingly beautiful prose in the whole novel. He details how he learned to understand language and emotion. How he marveled at the warmth of the sun, the blooming of flowers, the sweetness of fruit. How he grew to love the family he tenderly observed from his hiding place, and how devastating their rejection was. He explains how he came to know anger, loneliness, loss, rage—and the vengeful acts they inspired.

videos.title: Jev Course – Prefill-Only Inference & Decision Models from Scratch
videos.summary: Learn how to build high-speed decision-making pipelines for language models using Jev in PyTorch. This comprehensive course covers both encoder and decoder architectures, custom causal attention masking, and KV-cache reuse to bypass slow autoregressive generation.
body: ✏️ Course developed by Vivek Kalyanarangan.
📘 Author, Quantization and Fast Inference (Manning)
– 0:00:00 Introduction & Course Overview
points: Learn how to build high-speed decision-making pipelines for language models using Jev in PyTorch.
This comprehensive course covers both encoder and decoder architectures, custom causal attention masking, and KV-cache reuse to bypass slow autoregressive generation.
You will also explore fine-tuning techniques, teacher-student distillation, and reinforcement learning methods like GRPO to optimize decision latency and accuracy.
– 0:01:12 What is Jev & LLM Prefill vs. Decode
